procedures.checklist_entry: MPPT is protected from battery balance lead
procedures.procedure_description: Ensure the mppt is covered so that the battery balance lead cannot touch it.
Confirm the GPS module connector is fully seated and the GPS mast or mount is secure.

procedures.checklist_entry: All internal connectors connected, and no loose wires
procedures.procedure_description: All wires routed from the board are secured and cannot contact rotating parts or snag during flight.
Confirm the electronics board is fixed to the airframe with no rocking or vibration play.

procedures.checklist_entry: Close fuselage, and ensure fuselage screws are tight
procedures.procedure_description: Verify all fuselage screws are tightened to the specified torque value.
Verify all three phase wires between ESC and motor are connected and matched colour-to-colour to ensure correct motor rotation direction.
Insert the tail boom fully into the fuselage socket until it bottoms out. No gap should be visible at the interface.
Torque the retention screw(s) at the fuselage–boom interface to the specified value. Confirm no rotation or pull-out under firm hand pressure.
Inspect the fuselage socket and boom tube for visible cracks or delamination before and after tightening.

procedures.checklist_entry: No pinched wires at boom interface
procedures.procedure_description: Before seating the boom fully, confirm all tail servo wiring is routed through or alongside the boom without being pinched in the joint.
Insert each wing panel until the root seats flush against the fuselage. Confirm retention pins or latches are engaged.
Confirm the telemetry radio connector is fully mated. Verify antenna is attached and correctly oriented.
Position ELRS antennas per the installation guide (typically one horizontal, one vertical, or both angled at 90° to each other) for optimal link diversity.
Confirm the airspeed sensor is securely mounted and all connectors are fully mated.
Mate the aileron servo connector at the wing root for each wing. Confirm fully seated and locked.
Attach the horizontal stabiliser and fin per the tail assembly procedure. Confirm all attachment points are engaged.
Attach the horizontal stabiliser and fin per the tail assembly procedure. Confirm all attachment points are engaged.
Attach both wingtips to the outboard wing panels and confirm connectors inside the joint are mated before closing.

procedures.checklist_entry: Solar connectors & servos connected at wing tips
procedures.procedure_description: Pass the solar panel wiring through the designated root channel. Confirm connectors are accessible and not kinked or strained.
Apply securing tape over both wingtip joints to prevent in-flight separation.

procedures.checklist_entry: No major cracks, dents, or deformation (fuselage, wings, tail)
procedures.procedure_description: Perform a full visual inspection of all structural surfaces. Pay attention to high-stress areas: wing roots, spar tubes, tail boom join, and motor mount.
Check all control surface hinges for cracks, delamination, or missing material. Surfaces should pivot without any rocking perpendicular to the hinge line.
Hold each control surface and check for free play at the horn, clevis, and pushrod connections. Correct any play exceeding the maintenance manual limit.

procedures.checklist_entry: Motor securely mounted (no cracks in motor mount)
procedures.procedure_description: Attempt to rock the motor by hand. No movement should be detectable at the mount plate. Check for fretting marks or loose fasteners.
Inspect blade faces for cracks, nicks, or delamination. Confirm prop is seated flush on the shaft and the retaining nut is torqued correctly.
Inspect the motor mount plate and surrounding structure for cracks, particularly around fastener holes.

procedures.checklist_entry: No major damage on solar panels
procedures.procedure_description: Inspect all panel surfaces for cracked cells, deep scratches, or delamination of the encapsulant. Minor surface marks are acceptable; structural damage is not.
Wipe the solar panel surface with a clean dry cloth to remove dust and debris that would reduce power generation.

procedures.checklist_entry: Battery lead is isolated (prevent short circuit)
procedures.procedure_description: With all personnel clear of the propeller arc, connect the main flight battery. Stand by for autopilot boot sequence.
Place the flight battery (and any payload) in their intended positions before performing the CG check. Do not connect power yet.
Balance the aircraft at the CG datum points. Adjust battery position fore or aft as required until CG falls within the published limits.
Power on the RC transmitter first and confirm the correct model profile is loaded and throttle is at minimum.
Activate the kill switch to the safe position before connecting power, ensuring the motor cannot spin during power-up.
With all personnel clear of the propeller arc, connect the main flight battery. Stand by for autopilot boot sequence.

procedures.checklist_entry: Telemetry connected and GCS receiving data
procedures.procedure_description: Confirm the GCS telemetry link is active and parameters are streaming. No long gaps or timeout warnings.
Check RC link RSSI on the GCS or transmitter. Signal must be above the minimum acceptable threshold defined in the SOP.
Confirm the GCS shows the expected battery voltage for the state of charge. Cross-check against a cell voltage reading if available.
Wait for a stable 3D GPS fix with HDOP below 1.5 and at least 10 satellites. Confirm home position is set at the launch point.
Cycle through each mode switch position on the transmitter and confirm the GCS reports the expected flight modes as defined in the mission plan.
Verify RC loss failsafe and GCS disconnect failsafe are set to the approved actions (e.g. RTL, loiter, or continue mission) consistent with the OpSpec.
With transmitter sticks centred and autopilot initialised, confirm elevator, rudder, and ailerons are at or very close to neutral. Adjust trims or subtrim as needed.
With transmitter sticks centred and autopilot initialised, confirm elevator, rudder, and ailerons are at or very close to neutral. Adjust trims or subtrim as needed.
In MANUAL mode apply each stick input and verify correct surface response: pull back = elevator up; right rudder = rudder right; right stick = right aileron up / left aileron down.
Switch to FBWA and physically bank/pitch the airframe. Autopilot must deflect surfaces to oppose the movement: roll right = left aileron up; pitch nose up = elevator down.
Sweep each surface through its full travel. Movement must be smooth throughout the range with no buzzing, binding, or mid-travel resistance.

procedures.checklist_entry: No slip in control rod linkage
procedures.procedure_description: With servos active, apply firm hand pressure to each control surface. No movement should occur — any deflection indicates a slipping servo horn, loose clevis, or worn linkage.
Confirm the MPPT controller is powered and reporting on the GCS or dedicated monitoring interface.
Confirm the MPPT controller is powered and reporting on the GCS or dedicated monitoring interface.
